claims.text: On 25 June 2026 a magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck 16 km SW of Moron in northern Venezuela, west of Caracas.

OCHA's Situation Report #22 (15 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,829 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

OCHA's Situation Report #23 (16 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,930 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes, with more than 1,308 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. The additional appeal was raised to US$299 million, still targeting 1.3 million people over six months. EU Commissioner for Crisis Management Hadja Lahbib conducted a field visit to La Guaira together with the UN Humanitarian Coordinator to review response efforts.

OCHA's Situation Report #24 (17 July 2026, 8:00 pm) states that, twenty-three days since the earthquakes, authorities report an official toll of 5,069 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,331 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report #26 (19 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 5,208 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 1,388 aftershocks recorded since the 24 June earthquakes. An additional appeal for US$299 million remains in place to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months, on top of the US$632 million 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan.

Situation Report No. 28, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 21 July 2026, Time: 9:00 pm. Authorities report 1,405 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,346 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. The US$299 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan complements the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan, increasing the target population from 5.5 million to 6.2 million people and raising total funding requirements from US$632 million to US$931 million.

Situation Report No. 30, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 23 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm. Authorities report 1,463 aftershocks since the 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes that struck on 24 June. Official toll: 5,398 people dead and 16,740 injured. Authorities also indicated that 17,907 people lost their homes. Starting with this edition, the report will be published on a weekly basis. The next edition will be released on 30 July.

OCHA Situation Report #31, Earthquakes in Venezuela, 31 July 2026, 5:00 pm: authorities report 1,500 aftershocks since the 24 June doublet earthquakes (magnitude 7.2 and 7.5). Official toll: 5,546 people dead and 16,740 injured; 17,907 people lost their homes. As of 30 July, 207,700 people (54% women and girls) have accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance. The additional US$299 million appeal remains in place, complementing the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan for combined requirements of US$931 million targeting 6.2 million people, of whom 1.3 million are earthquake-affected. The report continues to be published weekly.
Re-checked 2 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026) remains the latest in its series; no Situation Report #32 has been published as of 2 August 2026, and figures are unchanged.
Re-checked 3 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026) remains the latest in its series; no Situation Report #32 has been published as of 3 August 2026, and figures are unchanged.

Re-checked 5 August 2026: IOM's Earthquake Response Situation Report #19 (covering 31 July - 3 August 2026, published 4 August 2026) reports ongoing shelter and relief operations -- including 796 people from 221 households sheltering at the Jose Maria Vargas Sports Complex and cumulative distributions of 4,987 kitchen sets, 4,580 tarpaulins, 3,441 solar lamps, 3,313 water containers and 2,527 hygiene kits -- but does not include a death toll or injury figure. OCHA's 'Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report' series remains at #31 (31 July 2026), with no #32 yet published; the official toll therefore remains unchanged at 5,546 dead and 16,740 injured.
The USGS is assessing earthquake-triggered landslide hazards generated by the 2026 Venezuela earthquake sequence.

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: OCHA's 'Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #31' (31 July 2026) remains the latest OCHA sitrep, confirming 'As of 24 July, authorities reported 5,546 deaths and 16,740 injuries.' IOM's Earthquake Response Situation Report #19 (31 July-3 August 2026, posted 4 August) remains the latest IOM report; no OCHA Situation Report #32 or IOM #20 has been published.

International Medical Corps' Venezuela Earthquakes Situation Report #5 (published 6 August 2026 on ReliefWeb) states: 'Official figures have confirmed 6,125 fatalities, 16,740 injuries and 17,907 people who have lost their homes' -- an increase in the confirmed death toll from the 5,546 recorded in OCHA Situation Report #31 (31 July 2026), while injury and homelessness figures are unchanged.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: OCHA's numbered 'Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report' series has resumed and caught up to the higher toll -- Situation Report #32 (7 August 2026, 2:00 pm) states: "As of 03 August, authorities reported 6,125 deaths and 16,740 injuries resulting from the earthquakes. They also reported that 60,992 people received care at hospitals and 43,679 homes were evaluated, out of which 6,433 are at high risk... 16,51% of the total rubble has been cleared... nearly 212,000 people had access to essential services and humanitarian assistance," with 24,477 of 28,223 temporary-camp capacity occupied. This directly confirms, via OCHA's own series, the 6,125 death toll previously reported only by International Medical Corps; injuries (16,740) and people who lost their homes (17,907) are unchanged.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #32 (7 August 2026) remains the latest in its numbered series; no Situation Report #33 has been published. It reiterates "6,125 deaths and 16,740 injuries resulting from the earthquakes" and states 43,679 homes have been evaluated, of which 6,433 are at high risk.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #32 (7 August 2026) remains the latest in its numbered series; no Situation Report #33 has been published. The ReliefWeb disaster update stream's newest item is Spanish-language response-coordination meeting minutes (6 August 2026) with no new figures. SitRep #32 continues to state 6,125 deaths and 16,740 injuries, with 43,679 homes evaluated of which 6,433 are at high risk.

Re-checked 11 August 2026: reliefweb.int, this record's live_source_url and the source of the numbered OCHA Situation Report series, returned HTTP 403 Forbidden and was unreachable across multiple attempts and multiple pages (disaster hub, specific SitRep #32 page, API endpoint) today. As an alternate allowlisted check, a UN News Venezuela article (16 July 2026, on IOM's El Nino warning for displaced families) was re-fetched directly and contains no death-toll or displacement figure newer than what is already on file. A web search surfaced non-allowlisted media reports (Al Jazeera, Jamaica Observer) of a Venezuelan National Assembly announcement putting the toll at 6,301 deaths as of 10 August 2026, but this could not be confirmed via any accessible allowlisted source today. The confirmed toll of 6,125 deaths and 16,740 injured (OCHA Situation Report #32, 7 August 2026) is retained unchanged pending restored ReliefWeb access.

Re-checked 12 August 2026: reliefweb.int and unocha.org both returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on every attempted URL again today (disaster page, OCHA Situation Report #32 page, WFP Situation Report #08, and the raw ReliefWeb API endpoint), the second consecutive day of being unreachable. USGS's event page remains fetchable but is a JS application with no extractable casualty data. The confirmed toll (6,125 deaths, 16,740 injured, per OCHA Situation Report #32, 7 August 2026) is retained unchanged pending restored ReliefWeb/OCHA access.

Re-checked 13 August 2026: reliefweb.int and unocha.org both returned HTTP 403 today (a third/fourth consecutive day); UN News's 16 July 2026 story contains no death toll newer than its original stale figure, and USGS does not publish an official death toll for this event. Figures (6,125 deaths, 16,740 injured, 17,907 displaced, per OCHA Situation Report #32, 7 August 2026) remain the latest confirmed via an allowlisted source; an unverified, non-allowlisted press figure of 6,301 deaths (Venezuela's National Assembly, 10 August 2026) remains unconfirmed.

Re-checked 14 August 2026: reliefweb.int and its report pages returned HTTP 403 for a fifth consecutive day; WebSearch surfaced references to newer-numbered ReliefWeb situation reports (e.g. Situation Report #6, 12 August; IOM Situation Report #21, 7-10 August) but their content could not be fetched from an allowlisted source to confirm figures. The confirmed toll (6,125 deaths, 16,740 injured, 17,907 displaced, per OCHA Situation Report #32, 7 August 2026) remains the latest allowlisted-confirmed figure; unconfirmed non-allowlisted press reports of a higher toll (~6,300) remain unconfirmed.

OCHA Situation Report #33 (14 August 2026, 14:00 local time): 'As of 10 August, authorities reported 6,301 deaths from the earthquakes,' 73,356 people received hospital care, 53,314 homes evaluated (9,567 at high risk), and about 23.26% of total rubble cleared; preliminary UNDRR estimates put direct damage to housing/infrastructure at approximately US$37 billion, while UNDP estimates direct physical damages at US$6.7 billion (6% of GDP); over 304,000 people (57% women and girls) had accessed essential services and humanitarian assistance as of 14 August, with the response scaling up to address 1.3 million people affected over the next six months.

As of 1 July 2026, nearly 2,000 deaths have been confirmed and more than 6,400 people rescued; 1.8 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance including 680,000 children across six affected states, with around 1,000 buildings and over 400 schools damaged and more than 600 aftershocks recorded since the initial quakes.

OCHA's Situation Report #14 (07 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,685 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes. Authorities also reported that approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and that more than 1,076 aftershocks have been recorded, with at least seven (7) states impacted and La Guaira remaining the most affected state.

OCHA's Situation Report #15 (08 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report an official toll of 3,811 people dead and 16,740 injured, with 6,462 people rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; approximately 17,907 people lost their homes and more than 1,100 aftershocks have been recorded. An additional appeal for US$296 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response for 1.3 million people over the next six months.

A first assessment by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) estimates direct physical damage to housing and infrastructure at some $37 billion, comprising $24 billion in damage to buildings and another $13 billion in infrastructure; at least 79 transitional camps have opened in stadiums and sports centres, hosting displaced residents and providing aid.

OCHA's Situation Report #18 (11 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that seventeen days after the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,333 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency; 1,171 aftershocks have been recorded, 17,907 people remain without housing, and 315 of those who died have yet to be identified. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher concluded his four-day visit to the country and called for sustained international support for the Humanitarian Response Plan; an additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.

OCHA's Situation Report No. 20 (13 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that, nineteen days since the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of 4,561 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the onset of the emergency, with more than 1,254 aftershocks recorded and 17,907 people remaining without housing. Authorities report at least 856 affected buildings, including 190 that have collapsed. The response continues with 107 transitional camps supporting affected populations, with a capacity of 25,064 people and a current occupancy of 20,231 people. A preliminary UNDP estimate indicates direct physical damage of US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 percent of GDP, alongside the earlier UNDRR estimate of approximately US$37 billion. The Government of Venezuela announced the creation of an initial reconstruction fund equivalent to US$200 million.

OCHA's Situation Report #21 (14 July 2026, 9:00 pm) states that authorities report a toll of 4,734 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued since the 24 June earthquakes; 17,907 people remain without housing.

description: A magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck northern Venezuela west of Caracas on 25 June 2026, 39 seconds after a magnitude 7.2 foreshock in the same sequence. The USGS assessed that high casualties and widespread damage are probable, and the national government of Venezuela declared a state of emergency. Five weeks on, the confirmed death toll has continued to climb past 5,540, and the UN humanitarian response has shifted toward a longer-term, multi-month recovery phase, with combined funding requirements exceeding $900 million. Re-checked 10 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #32 (7 August 2026) remains the latest in its numbered series; no Situation Report #33 has been published, and the confirmed toll of 6,125 deaths and 16,740 injuries is unchanged. The confirmed toll (6,125 deaths, 16,740 injured, per OCHA SitRep #32, 7 August 2026) is retained unchanged. Re-checked 13 August 2026: reliefweb.int and unocha.org both returned HTTP 403 today (a third/fourth consecutive day); UN News's 16 July 2026 story contains no death toll newer than its original stale figure, and USGS does not publish an official death toll for this event. Figures (6,125 deaths, 16,740 injured, 17,907 displaced, per OCHA Situation Report #32, 7 August 2026) remain the latest confirmed via an allowlisted source; an unverified, non-allowlisted press figure of 6,301 deaths (Venezuela's National Assembly, 10 August 2026) remains unconfirmed. Re-checked 14 August 2026: reliefweb.int returned HTTP 403 for a fifth consecutive day; newer-numbered ReliefWeb report titles were found via search but not fetchable to confirm figures. The confirmed toll (6,125 deaths, 16,740 injured, 17,907 displaced, per OCHA Situation Report #32, 7 August 2026) remains the latest allowlisted-confirmed figure. Re-checked 15 August 2026: reliefweb.int and unocha.org both returned HTTP 403 for a sixth consecutive day; a search-indexed title suggesting a newer, differently-numbered 'Earthquake Response Situation Report #22' could not be opened or verified. The confirmed toll (6,125 deaths, 16,740 injured, 17,907 displaced, per OCHA Situation Report #32, 7 August 2026) remains the latest allowlisted-confirmed figure. Re-checked 16 August 2026: OCHA Situation Report #33 (14 August) confirms the death toll at 6,301 (reported by authorities as of 10 August), with 73,356 people having received hospital care and 53,314 homes evaluated (9,567 at high risk); damage estimates range from US$6.7 billion (UNDP) to US$37 billion (UNDRR). Over 304,000 of an estimated 1.3 million affected people have received assistance so far, with the response explicitly still scaling up and planning extending six months forward.
